snippets.text: Von Hippel Lindau syndrome is an autosomal dominant hereditary syndrome manifested by a variety of benign and malignant tumors, including the central nervous system, retinal hemangioblastoma, pheochromocytoma, and neuroendocrine tumors of the pancreas. The syndrome affects 1 per 36,000 people in the general population. The chances of developing pheochromocytoma are 25%-30%. There is a difference between type 1, which involves a low risk of developing pheochromocytoma, and type 2, in which pheochromocytoma often occurs. These are mostly adrenal, and in 50% of the cases, bilateral.

snippets.text: The incidence and prevalence of acute pericarditis are unknown, and many cases are considered to go undiagnosed. One study showed that acute pericarditis might account for up to 5% of presentation to the emergency department and account for 0.1% of admissions for chest pain.[1] Typically, the demographic affected are men aged between 20 to 50 years old.[2]
